result.title: Beyond Visual Fidelity: Comparing Categorical and Continuous World Models
result.summary: Visual world models can now generate compelling interactive worlds, but visual realism does not guarantee faithful dynamics. We systematically compare how categorical and continuous prediction shape learned dynamics under both next-token and iterative whole-frame generation. These choices are often bundled in approaches such as autoregressive token models and whole-frame flow matching. We design controlled 2D and 3D environments and evaluate dynamics validity, calibration, and visual quality. In 2D with lossless visual encoding, categorical models achieve higher rollout validity with less training compute, particularly for stochastic entities. Among categorical models, greedy decoding produces the highest rollout validity, while sampling from a next-token model yields the best-calibrated stochastic predictions. Failures in continuous models, such as disappearing game characters, echo those seen in more complex environments. Here, known dynamics let us measure their impact. In 3D, categorical models also achieve stronger long-horizon performance with less training compute. Even models with lossy tokenization remain competitive on semantic accuracy and FVD, despite lower next-frame RGB accuracy. Together, these findings make a strong case for categorical prediction as a compute-efficient route to learning world dynamics.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在受控2D/3D环境中系统比较离散类别预测与连续预测（next-token 自回归 vs 整帧迭代 flow matching）对动力学学习的影响，评测 rollout 有效性、校准与视觉质量，发现离散模型以更少训练算力取得更高长时程有效性。
AI.relevance_reason: 离散 token 与连续 latent 的状态生成、贪心解码与采样对校准的差异、以及有损视觉编码在语义指标上仍具竞争力，可为 LVR 中推理状态表示与生成范式的选择提供待核查的旁证线索，但其世界模型设定能否迁移到推理状态仍需阅读原文判断。
